newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors split on PepsiCo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors split on PepsiCo.

text.p: Options investors appeared split over the prospects of PepsiCo Inc as the stock rallied sharply on a report the company may be set to spin off its $11 billion restaurant business, traders said Thursday.
The company said its board of directors was scheduled to meet Thursday but declined to say whether a spinoff was on the agenda.
By 1215 CST/1815 GMT, PepsiCo shares were up 2-1/2 at 34-1/2 on volume of more than 24.5 million shares in consolidated trading.
"I'm trading big size both ways," a trader at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said of PepsiCo options. "There's definitely interest every way."
He said investors were exiting some long positions and opening new positions, both on the put and call side.
"Two-way paper means people are buying puts and selling calls too," said Todd Salamone, senior analyst at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute.
"The fact there is two-way paper on such a pop would have bullish implications for the stock," he said.

The PepsiCo February 32-1/2 put was the most active in the group, with volume of roughly 3,435 contracts. The option, which had open interest of just 179 contracts through Wednesday, was down 3/4 at 3/8.
Also on the put side, the February 30 traded about 1,530 contracts and the April 35 traded about 1,130.
Among the calls, the March 35, which was up 1-5/16 at 1-5/8, was most active, with volume of 2,675.
Other active calls included the February 30 and 32-1/2, the April 30 and 35 and the July 32-1/2.
The trader said volatilities rose slightly.
"Volatility is up about two points, to about 28 to 30," he said, adding that orders were coming from both retail and institutional investors.
"There's enormous retail business," he added. "I think people are taking shots on some of the calls hoping this is a $45 deal and not a $35 deal."
Salamone said the stock's move through the 33 region, which stopped an upturn last November, was positive but that supply could emerge in the 36 area, where the shares topped out in July last year.
"We could see some potential supply coming in there," he said. "People that were holding the shares at 36 when it dropped back to 29 might be thinking they can break even here."
